[Fix][Benchmark] Let the native full-duplex oracle accept a truncate grant (#3248)

MiniCPM-o's full-duplex sessions now grant supports_truncate, so the protocol
oracle failed every native Full-Duplex-Bench session on that grant, although
the recorder never sends a truncate. The native profile no longer pins it, as
the turn-based profile already leaves it to the deployment.

Co-authored-by: Eric(Qun) <186020953+0xtoward@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
[Fix] Keep TP ranks paired when a fanned-out request is aborted (#3233)

A stage whose scheduler takes replicated TP work, such as the Ming-Omni
image encoder with image_encoder.tp_size 2 or 4, lets every rank decide
on its own whether to skip an aborted request. The leader writes work
and aborts to separate follower queues, a follower drops work that
arrives after its abort, and each rank's scheduler skips a queued
request once its abort lands. When the ranks reach that point at
different times, one rank runs the aborted request while another moves
on, so two different requests meet in one collective and the next
request returns a wrong result or times out.

The leader still drops a request it sees aborted before fanout. After
fanout, every rank runs the request to completion and the leader stage
suppresses its output, so a follower runs all work it receives and TP
fanout ranks no longer forward the abort to their scheduler.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ["leader", "follower"])
+def test_tp_rank_runs_fanned_out_work_after_abort(role: str) -> None:
+    async def run() -> None:
+        scheduler = SimpleScheduler(lambda payload: payload)
+        stage = make_stage(role=role, scheduler=scheduler, tp_fanout=Mock())
+        payload = make_stage_payload(request_id="req-1")
+        if role == "leader":
+            await stage.execute(payload)
+            stage.on_abort("req-1")
+        else:
+            stage.on_abort("req-1")
+            await stage.execute(payload)
+        threading.Thread(target=scheduler.start, daemon=True).start()
+        try:
+            assert scheduler.outbox.get(timeout=5).request_id == "req-1"
+        finally:
+            scheduler.stop()
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
